:::{#cor-log-recip}
#### Logarithm of a reciprocal

If $a > 0$,
then the [natural logarithm](#def-natural-log) of $\frac{1}{a}$ is the negative of the natural logarithm of $a$:

$$\logf{\frac{1}{a}} = -\logf{a}$$

:::

{{< slidebreak >}}

::: proof

Since $1 > 0$ and $a > 0$,
@cor-log-quot applies to the [quotient](algebra-sums.qmd#def-quotient) $\frac{1}{a}$:

$$
\ba
\logf{\frac{1}{a}}
&= \logf{1} - \logf{a}
&& \text{(logarithm of a quotient)}
\\
&= 0 - \logf{a}
&& \text{(} \logf{1} = 0 \text{)}
\\
&= -\logf{a}
&& \text{(} 0 - c = -c \text{)}
\ea
$$

The first step applies @cor-log-quot,
and the second uses $\logf{1} = 0$ from @exm-natural-log.

:::
